title: Design System: chatSaaS — The Operator's Board

patch-amber.note: Surface-only amber: live jack body, live pill dot/border, current stepper waypoint, live ring shadow. Never text on ivory (~3:1).

patch-amber-deep.note: The text-safe amber (contrast fix from the finish review): amber labels and filled primary control grounds; clears 4.5:1 on ivory.

operators-ivory.note: Page ground; text on filled controls; the pinhole in every jack; selection foreground.

panel-warm.note: Card surface, one bright step above the ground: cards, dialog panels, inputs, snippet boxes.

well-warm.note: Inset well, one warm step below the ground: meter/progress channels, drag-over, hover and selected grounds.

slate-ink.note: Primary text, unlit jack bodies, ink fills and ink plug, focus outline, selection background, 40% dialog overlay.

hairline-slate.note: All 1px borders and dividers; dashed dropzone outline; unwired stepper cords; thin scrollbars.

display.purpose: Page titles only — 'Your lines', 'Plan & credits' (text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight).

title.purpose: Section subheads and card names in Inter; bot names on jacks use the Label voice instead.

body.purpose: Helper text and descriptions at 70–80% ink, relaxed leading.

label.purpose: Engraved-plate mono: jack names, pills, buttons, nav, readouts (tabular-nums for numbers).

shadows.name: live-jack
shadows.purpose: The ONLY shadow in the system — the amber ring on a lit jack at publish. 2px offset + 12px blur (never a flat halo).

motion.name: jack-click
motion.purpose: The one authored motion (ADR-007): the patch-cord click when a line is plugged in at publish — and on the embed jack after a successful copy. Opt-in only (justPlugged); the board never animates for decoration.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Header gaps tighten below sm so the compact credits pill fits.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Below md the meter card hides; the credits position rides the header as a compact ink pill.

structure.focusRing: 2px solid var(--color-slate-ink) outline, 2px offset, border-radius falls back to var(--radius-plate, 6px)
structure.selection: Slate Ink background, Operator's Ivory text

components.name: Plug — primary
components.description: The plug: primary create/publish control. Patch Amber Deep ground, ivory mono label. Only where a line is actually plugged in.
components.css: .ds-plug-primary { background: var(--color-patch-amber-deep, #8a6508); color: var(--color-operators-ivory, #f8f4e9); border: none; border-radius: var(--radius-plug, 9999px); padding: 10px 20px; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s; } .ds-plug-primary:hover { background: rgb(138 101 8 / 0.9); } .ds-plug-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-plug-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.6; }

components.name: Plug — ink
components.description: The workhorse pill: step continues, Copy snippet, Unplug, login. Slate Ink ground, ivory mono label.
components.css: .ds-plug-ink { background: var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); color: var(--color-operators-ivory, #f8f4e9); border: none; border-radius: var(--radius-plug, 9999px); padding: 10px 20px; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s; } .ds-plug-ink:hover { background: rgb(45 49 66 / 0.9); } .ds-plug-ink:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-plug-ink:disabled { opacity: 0.6; }

components.description: Cancel, dismiss, Try again, Go to plan. Panel Warm ground, hairline border, ink mono label; hover settles on Well Warm.

components.name: Text input
components.description: Board input: Panel Warm ground, hairline border, 14px card radius. Placeholder and text in ink.
components.css: .ds-input { background: var(--color-panel-warm, #fdfbf4); color: var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); border: 1px solid var(--color-hairline-slate, #d6d2c4); border-radius: var(--radius-card, 14px); padding: 12px 16px; font-family: var(--font-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 16px; width: 100%; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: rgb(45 49 66 / 0.7); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Line-state pill
components.description: The four-state line vocabulary (Unplugged / Connecting / Live / On hold). Live is the only amber state; others stay achromatic.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; border: 1px solid var(--color-hairline-slate, #d6d2c4); border-radius: var(--radius-plate, 6px); padding: 4px 10px; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); } .ds-pill-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: var(--radius-jack, 9999px); background: rgb(45 49 66 / 0.4); } .ds-pill--live { border-color: var(--color-patch-amber, #b8860b); color: var(--color-patch-amber-deep, #8a6508); } .ds-pill--live .ds-pill-dot { background: var(--color-patch-amber, #b8860b); }

components.name: Jack card
components.description: The labeled jack row: circular jack (44px, ivory pinhole), engraved-plate bot name, trailing state pill. Flat card; the only shadow lives on the lit jack. The just-plugged click plays once via .ds-jack--clicked.
components.html:
Front desk answers

components.css: .ds-jack-card { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; background: var(--color-panel-warm, #fdfbf4); border: 1px solid var(--color-hairline-slate, #d6d2c4); border-radius: var(--radius-card, 14px); font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); } .ds-card-pill { margin-left: auto; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; border: 1px solid var(--color-hairline-slate, #d6d2c4); border-radius: var(--radius-plate, 6px); padding: 4px 10px; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-card-pill-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: var(--radius-jack, 9999px); background: rgb(45 49 66 / 0.4); } .ds-card-pill--live { border-color: var(--color-patch-amber, #b8860b); color: var(--color-patch-amber-deep, #8a6508); } .ds-card-pill--live .ds-card-pill-dot { background: var(--color-patch-amber, #b8860b); } @keyframes ds-jack-click { 0% { transform: scale(0.85); box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgb(184 134 11 / 0); } 55% { transform: scale(1.06); box-shadow: 0 2px 18px 0 rgb(184 134 11 / 0.45); } 100% { transform: scale(1); box-shadow: var(--shadow-live-jack, 0 2px 12px 0 rgb(184 134 11 / 0.35)); } } .ds-jack--clicked { animation: ds-jack-click 450ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) 1; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-jack--clicked { animation: none; components.name: Create-flow stepper
components.description: Four cord waypoints (name → documents → review → publish). Current step carries Patch Amber — the plug path; the cord is ink once wired, hairline ahead.
components.html:
1. Name
  2. Documents
  3. Review
  4. Publish
components.css: .ds-stepper { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; width: 100%; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; } .ds-step { flex: 1; } .ds-step:last-child { flex: 0; } .ds-step-dot { display: inline-block; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: var(--radius-jack, 9999px); border: 2px solid var(--color-hairline-slate, #d6d2c4); background: transparent; vertical-align: middle; } .ds-step-dot--complete { border-color: var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); background: var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); } .ds-step-dot--current { border-color: var(--color-patch-amber, #b8860b); background: var(--color-patch-amber, #b8860b); } .ds-step-cord { display: inline-block; height: 1px; flex: 1; background: var(--color-hairline-slate, #d6d2c4); vertical-align: middle; } .ds-step-cord--wired { background: var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); } .ds-step-label { display: block; margin-top: 8px; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-slate-ink, #2d3142); } .ds-step-label--current { color: var(--color-patch-amber-deep, #8a6508); } .ds-step-label--future { color: rgb(45 49 66 / 0.7); }

narrative.overview:
chatSaaS is a switchboard. The operator — a non-technical small-business owner — plugs a customer's question into their knowledge by connecting two jacks, and the line goes live. The managed infrastructure (the rack, the routing, the machines) is real but invisible; the operator only ever sees labeled jacks, a patch cord, and a lit line. The interface is a calm instrument panel: warm ivory ground, deep slate ink, and a single warm accent that appears only where a line is actually live. Every state reads instantly from the panel's own vocabulary — unplugged, connecting, live, on hold — never from jargon.

This is a workhorse surface, not a spectacle. The visitor came to operate: create a chatbot from their documents, publish it to their site, and know exactly where they stand against their plan and credits. Density is generous and unhurried; nothing glitters except the moment a line goes live. The register is trustworthy, warm, and engineered to feel like a well-kept machine room rather than a startup dashboard. The build landed as committed, with two recorded adaptations: depth is carried by a two-step tonal layering (Panel Warm cards on the ivory ground, Well Warm for inset wells — Panel Warm #FDFBF4, Well Warm #EDE7D3), and amber gained a second, darker step (Patch Amber Deep #8A6508) because raw amber on ivory fails the 4.5:1 contrast floor for text and filled controls. Raw Patch Amber stays surface-only; Deep is the amber that speaks.
keyCharacteristics: One warm accent (amber) reserved for the live line; everything else stays achromatic.
Ivory/cream ground with deep slate ink — light, not dark, built for daytime office use (light scheme is pinned; no dark mode).
Inter for body and data; IBM Plex Mono labels with engraved-plate letter spacing (0.08em).
Two-step tonal layering instead of shadows: Panel Warm cards on the ivory ground, Well Warm wells; exactly one shadow in the system.
Generous rhythm and quiet density; the interface recedes until a line is live.
Every bot is a labeled jack on a board; states are line states, never status widgets.

rules.name: The Live Line Rule
rules.body: Patch Amber appears only on the line that is active: the lit jack of a published bot, the primary create/publish control, the create flow's current waypoint (the plug path — sanctioned by the WI-007 visual contract, Task 8), and the live pill. Raw amber is surface-only; amber as text is always Patch Amber Deep. If amber covers more than a small fraction of a screen, the design has drifted.

rules.name: The Jack Label Rule
rules.body: Labels read like engraved plate: short, machine-precise, never sentence-long. A label that needs a paragraph is body copy, not a label.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. The only elevated moment in the system is the live jack at the moment a line is plugged in.

dos: Do keep Patch Amber rare and purposeful — the live jack, the plug control, the current waypoint, and the live pill only; raw amber surface-only, #8A6508 wherever amber must be text or a filled control.
Do keep every label and state in the operator's plain language; never expose cloud or infrastructure vocabulary.
Do read states from the line vocabulary (unplugged / connecting / live / on hold) rather than generic status widgets.
Do carry depth with the two-step tonal layering — Panel Warm #FDFBF4 for surfaces, Well Warm #EDE7D3 for wells, hovers, and selections.
Do keep browser surfaces in-world: ink selection, thin hairline scrollbars, light scheme pinned.
Do write all UI copy in English, per the product language commitment.
donts: Don't fall back to the generic blue SaaS dashboard — the ivory/slate/amber board is the committed world (the focus outline is ink, never the blue default).
Don't introduce green or red for status; the amber line and its state label carry meaning alone.
Don't add a second shadow or animate the board for decoration — the only shadow is the live jack's, and the only authored motion is the patch-cord click at publish/copy moments.
Don't set raw Patch Amber as text on ivory; it fails 4.5:1 — Patch Amber Deep exists for that.
Don't let the retro switchboard theme slip into kitsch — keep it engineered, calm, and restrained.
Don't use multiple accents; the system has one voice. And don't reach for window.confirm/alert — the in-world Dialog is the only confirmation surface.
